_docs: Design documents (read these before reworking either layer; paths relative to the project root, may have been moved or deleted since): Docs/ImagePortraits/Plan_ImageClassifier.md (the classifier tool: tagging, rules, Analyze/Classify, user decisions) and Docs/ImagePortraits/Plan_GlobalPortraitHandler.md (the in-game generated portrait handlers built from this file: findings, design, decisions D1-D32). Code: Assets/Editor/ImageClassifier/ (tool), Assets/Scripts/CharacterData/GlobalPortraitTemplate.cs + Character_Portraits.cs (game).
_doc_file: Two layers in one file. (1) The CLASSIFICATION rules for the editor tool Tools/Image Classifier (Docs/ImagePortraits/Plan_ImageClassifier.md): settings, excluded_tags, clause_aliases, files_category, file_name_variants, file_names, emotion_pass, portrait_emotions. Moved here from workingdir/Plans/Draft_ImageRules.json on 2026-10-17 (P3.5); the previous version of this file is workingdir/Plans/Image_Generation_Config.pre-P3.5.json. Located in Mods/Assetpacks/ so the game can read it at launch. (2) The DISPLAY layer portrait_global (see _doc_display_layer), read by the game, not by the tool.
_doc_data_driven: ALL classification logic lives in this file; the tool has no built-in categories, tags or names. To catch a new kind of image, add a files_category entry (and file_names entries if needed); to catch a new dataset's wording, add tags to the clauses. Every key below is read by the tool; unknown keys (other than _comments) are rule-check warnings in Analyze.
_syntax: Clause = OR of tags separated by |. An entry's clause array = AND. 'tag*0.5' scales that tag's score (weak or generic evidence). '$name' expands to clause_aliases[name]. 'none' = any of these tags above threshold rejects the entry. Pseudo-tags usable in any clause: 'rating:<general|sensitive|questionable|explicit>' (the tagger's rating head), 'face:<tag>' (WD14 on the face crop, emotion pass) and 'vlm:<label>' (1 when the emotion pass VLM answered that label). NAME ENTRIES: 'tier': the lowest tier whose best match reaches settings.tierMinScore (or the entry's own 'tierMinScore') wins - a stray lower-tier hint such as all_fours 0.42*0.5 = 0.21 cannot override fellatio 0.98 in a later tier; if no tier reaches it, the lowest matching tier wins; a winner below settings.minScore is low confidence; score only competes inside a tier; listed order breaks exact ties; tiers may be decimals (3.5) to insert one. 'hasVariants': variant ids from file_name_variants in priority order, the first that applies is appended as _<id>. 'fallback': true = only competes when no regular entry matched (other, generic). An entry with no clauses always matches with score 0. 'onlyInCategories' limits an entry to those categories. The same name may appear twice (alternative definitions). CATEGORY KEYS: all/any/none (clauses), threshold (tag threshold for this category's clauses, default settings.tagThreshold), group (consecutive matching categories with the same group compete: the highest any-clause score wins, listed order breaks ties - e.g. dog_penis 0.97 beats a stray horse_penis 0.63), hold (match = stop, image stays unmatched), nameSet (which name list names the image, default file_names), moveLowConfidence (default true), rename (false = category only, original file name kept), refines (an image sorted into that category's folder moves here when this rule's all/none clauses hold; its any clauses are not needed).
_doc_manual_changes: How Classify treats files you handled by hand: a file named in the final convention <name>_<parent>_<folder>_<N> is settled; restore its original name or rename it to anything else to classify it again. An image inside a category folder keeps that category (your sort or an earlier pass) and the rules only name it - except a refines move (horse -> horse_pov). allowedNames is an optional category-wide allowlist applied to BOTH filename and tag naming (tentacle inhibits all human positions). Images the tool placed that you moved out of category folders without renaming stay out. Moved or renamed files keep tags (matched by size + date); deleted files drop out. Restore every file's original name replaces pass-based undo: restore the immutable recorded basename in its CURRENT folder, never move it back to an old folder. Collisions, unsafe paths and changed files are reported and skipped, never overwritten. Analyze writes ONE _image_analysis.md with classified thumbnail clusters and uncertain diagnostics; legacy _unclassified.md is not rewritten. Analyze creates category and 'unsorted' folders; unsorted/ images are ignored by Tag/Analyze/Classify but may have their recorded original names restored. manual:true (human_female) categories are hand-sorted only. The report lists folder/rule disagreements.
_doc_display_layer: Two-layer design: this file also drives the DISPLAY layer, read by the game (GlobalPortraitTemplate, Docs/ImagePortraits/Plan_GlobalPortraitHandler.md), not by the tool. At every game start the game builds a global portrait template from files_category + file_names + file_name_variants + portrait_global; a character template opts in with Portrait.useGlobalHandler = [ { "path": "<character folder>", "selfKeys": [...] } ] (priority order; never saved). tagsMatch there are IN-GAME portrait keywords (blowjob, doggy, masturbate), NOT image tags. A new file_names entry needs a portrait_global.names entry (keywords with roles), or its images are never requested.
_excluded_tags_doc: Tags the tagger never stores, to keep _image_tags.jsonl small (e.g. hair colours, clothing, backgrounds no rule uses). Used by the next Tag run: new images are tagged without them and existing records are stripped of them, so the list can grow bit by bit without re-tagging. Excluding a tag that a rule uses is a rule-check warning in Analyze. Removing a tag from this list only brings it back for images tagged afterwards (use Re-tag all).
_filename_confidence_doc: A category with filenameFirst:true can be selected by a uniquely recognized source name before tag routing. Thus smiling selects portrait even with strong lactation tags; no Emotion_ prefix is consulted. Category tag disagreements remain informational for a filename-selected category. Without that override, filenameConfirmedNearMisses lists category near misses that become informational after name confirmation (portrait/human). Held unknown actors remain held, fixed category folders remain authoritative, and variant uncertainty remains visible.
_filename_hints_doc: Editor naming searches immutable originalName (or current basename for legacy records) for canonical ids and these aliases. Search is case-insensitive, punctuation-tolerant and bounded: FullNelson/full_nelson/full nelson agree, while oral cannot match coral and anal cannot match analysis. Explicit spelling aliases handle smiling rather than unrestricted substring matching. Longer containing matches win across name sets (golden shower -> pee, not shower); unrelated conflicting names retain tag-based routing. filenameFirst categories may override tag-selected categories; existing actor categories are retained for sexual action names, and manually fixed folders never change here. Configured filename_variant_hints can establish allowed variants; other variants use tags. filenameOnly entries never compete on tags. originalName survives moves, renames, retagging and undo. Runtime generated classification stays game/tag-driven.
_image_states_doc: Independent state after the normal variant: <action>[_<variant>][_mindcontrolled]_<pack>_<character>_<N>. Filename aliases (editor opt-in) OR tag clauses select the state without replacing action, actor category or variant. Runtime keywords are OR alternatives for the same pool; stateful assets are preferred only for matching requests, ordinary assets remain fallback. Plain expressionless/empty_eyes do not prove this state. No implicit inference from a folder name.

_character_emotions_doc: ComfyUI Character Selector only: manual emotion ID -> prompts plus optional requireActorTags (all), requireAnyActorTags (any), excludeActorTags (none). Guards use case-sensitive actor-profile !tag (absence) semantics and only the selected exported character's original actor_tags, never action flags. Unknown/ineligible selections are ignored. none is universal and adds nothing. actorTags/removeActorTags overlay a deep copy before all optional/body-token rule evaluation; unrelated real states remain, so sleeping and timestop can coexist. Expression prompts append only to main_naked_prompt and main_clothed_prompt with case-sensitive comma-tag deduplication; support_prompt is unchanged. custom_prompt appends literal temporary text only to those two main outputs and is preserved as custom_main_prompt metadata in the registered snapshot, never inserted into action or composition text. State overrides need a compatible character export with guarded __base__ rules (unconscious suppresses open eyes/halo and enables closed eyes/sleeping; timestop alone preserves eyes/halo). Legacy flattened prompts cannot truly override those states: re-export rather than deleting arbitrary prompt tokens.
_emotion_pass_doc: Images whose category is listed get a second pass during Tag (ComfyUI node MisteraFaceEmotion, workflow Assets/Editor/ImageClassifier/EmotionWorkflow_API.json): the face is cropped, WD14 tags the crop (rules: face:<tag>), and the VLM picks ONE of these labels for the crop (rules: vlm:<label>, score 1). Changing labels or prompt re-runs the pass on the next Tag.

emotion_pass._comment: Optional face crop + VLM pass deliberately disabled (categories empty). Portrait naming uses original filenames and conservative full-image WD14 fallbacks; existing face/VLM records may still contribute without requiring a new pass.
emotion_pass.prompt: Look at this anime character's face. Which ONE of these expressions fits best? {labels}. Answer with exactly one word from the list, nothing else.

_portrait_emotions_doc: Portrait category only. Filename-first against this nameSet: identifiable emotion source names keep distinct base ids; filenameOnly:true entries never participate in tag matching (empty clauses are NOT unconditional). No action/pose/graphic ids such as standing, bathe, dogeza, facetoface or cum. Tier 1 sleeping full-image evidence, tier 2 existing face tags, tier 3 existing VLM labels; the optional emotion pass remains disabled. Tier 4 alternative definitions provide conservative full-image WD14 fallback without a VLM dependency: specific emotion evidence only, not open_mouth/closed_mouth/blush/frown/body posture. Smile excludes conflicting negative/specific smiles. Weak scores remain low confidence and never move; unmatched portraits are not renamed. neutral is the baseline (default/expressionless filename aliases), not a catch-all classification.
_portrait_activities_doc: Nonsexual activities and source states, stored in activity/. Explicit filenames are authoritative; tag-only recognition requires activity evidence without sexual context. Gift direction and death are never inferred from generic holding, lying, closed eyes or sleeping. pee is available here for solo/nonsexual context and in file_names for sexual context.

_portrait_global_doc: Game only (GlobalPortraitTemplate). For every categories entry (priority order) and every roleBlocks entry (doer, receiver, none) one image handler: RequireSelfContextKeys = selfKeys, RequireTargetContextKeys = targetKeys. Its variants are the file_names entries whose keyword role matches the block (role both = receiver side from <category>/, doer side from <category>_perform/, hand-sorted): one variant per applicable variants entry ([keyword, variant keywords], see _variants_doc) and one base variant ([keyword], the variants.base files). The first names[].keywords pair is primary; later pairs are fallback-only. Entries with identical tagsMatch and primary/fallback status merge their image patterns. For an unimplemented position, put the implemented command keyword first so its assets join that command's primary pool, rather than being unreachable while the primary pool has images. Order inside a handler: more tagsMatch first, primary before fallback-only, then file_names tier. The none block ends with an unconditional variant (no tagsMatch) of the unconditional names. alsoUseFolders: extra category folders read by that category (human also uses pov). The two pov entries: first = player only (the game tags the player pov), second = no target requirement, generic fallback that also catches solo acts. Built at game launch and kept in the serializer; debugOutput: in the Unity editor the built template is also written next to this file.

portrait_global._emotions_doc: Dedicated portrait/ handler appended AFTER all action/sex handlers, with no role requirement. Keys are game expression keywords, arrays are ordered classified portrait_emotions base ids. Exact id variants for every emotion come first (including extended source ids); each fallback id is a separate later variant, never a pooled random choice. Unknown ids warn and are skipped. Patterns use all emotion ids to keep prefixes apart (happy vs happy_tears, crying vs crying_with_eyes_open). Only neutral is unconditional, at the very end. This does not classify action/graphic source names as emotions.

categories._comment: set 2: generic sex fallback, solo acts

portrait_global._variants_doc: Portrait variants of every name: id -> { keywords, files }. keywords = in-game portrait keywords added to the name's keyword (tagsMatch [doggy, anal, raped]). files = file suffixes shown, in order (the file name is <name>_<suffix>_<pack>_<chara>_<N>); "" = the unspecified files (no suffix). Eg. anal_rape [doggy, anal, raped] = doggystyle_anal_rape_* + doggystyle_anal_*. "base" = the variant without extra keywords ([doggy], and the none block's unconditional variant); vaginal has no game keyword, so its files go there. A variant applies to a name when one of its suffixes is in the name's hasVariants (file_names) or is a suffix the classifier never writes (named by hand, eg. anal_rape); a classifier suffix not in hasVariants is skipped for that name. Order in a handler: more keywords first, then this listed order. Variants with the same keywords merge their files (rape + vaginal_rape = [raped]). Every file_name_variants id must appear in some files list, or its images are never shown (warning at launch). Longer suffixes stay apart: the anal files are doggystyle_anal_* without doggystyle_anal_rape_*.
portrait_global._names_doc: file_names id -> keywords: OR list of { keyword, role }. keyword = in-game portrait keyword (null = no own keyword: the name is part of the none block's unconditional variant, only its keyworded variants get tags, eg. [sleeping]). role = block: doer / receiver / none / both (both = receiver side from <category>/, doer side from <category>_perform/). The first keyword is primary across roles: names with the same primary keyword, role, and variant tags pool their images. Later entries with a different keyword are fallback-only and are not used while a matching primary variant has images. Repeating the first keyword for another explicit role keeps it primary and uses ordinary category folders (spooning/intercrural). For unimplemented positions, put the implemented command keyword FIRST (prone_bone: doggy first, prone_bone second) so doggy can select both doggystyle and prone_bone assets. Once a dedicated command is implemented, its keyword can become primary if separate pools are desired. Cross-role mappings with different keywords (oral = blowjob doer OR irrumatio receiver) intentionally retain their separate priorities. Kept here, not in file_names: the classifier treats any extra key of a file_names entry as the name and skips the entry.

_prompt_scene_doc: Game only (ActionScenePromptUtility): generation rules reverse portrait_global (game tags -> prompts). Read on every build. Each raw source interaction has one doer, optional receiver, command tags, job tags and source-local actor tags; actors carry their short tags (girl / boy / futa or species). Clause arrays all/any/none use | for alternatives. Scene count tags include <short tag>:N, other:N, actors:N, doers:N and receivers:N; N+ means at least N. {count} counts futa as girl. Fixed root output order: composition, complete pair groups (relative pair prompt followed by child actions), actors (doers then receivers), room. There is no scene output section or configurable layout. The first selected option declaring view locks a coherent global view before rendering and sets result.pov; scene.usePov remains unchanged POV eligibility, exposed as pov_possible. Later camera choices must use that same view; other local groups may test view:pov / view:external. POV is declared by a camera option with view: pov and literal pov in its prompts, never by a scene rule, semantic {pov} marker or camera cleanup. POV omits the player's actor section. Source matching sees scene-wide pov_possible eligibility, not unrelated action flags.
_prompt_derived_tags_doc: Derive tags in order on each raw source interaction, using only its doer / receiver and source tags. all/any/none are source conditions; doer / receiver are side-local clause blocks; differs requires each clause to match exactly one side (| groups alternatives before comparing). bestiality and futa_with_female are source-local flags, never recomputed from unrelated scene actors. futa_with_female uses two directional rules for an actual futa and female pairing. Scene and composite aggregation unions flags from actual matched sources only; it must not infer a pairing from global actor flags. Later derivations see earlier additions.

prompt_derived_tags._comment: one side black, the other not
an animal (race type animal: horse, dog, pig, bear) on one side only

_prompt_pair_derived_tags_doc: Run in listed order for each ActionScenePair before prompt_pair_rules; later entries see earlier additions. SceneDerivedTag-compatible entries: add is a tag list; all/any/none are clause lists on pair-local tags (the grouped actions and its actors), main/support are { all, any, none } blocks on that actor only, pairKind selects distinct / self / solo. differs is an AND list of clauses: each clause must match exactly one actor; | groups alternatives BEFORE comparing sides, so differs [petite1|petite2] does not match petite1 versus petite2. Pair flags must be derived locally, not borrowed from unrelated scene-wide interactions. Relative derivations require pairKind distinct: self has the same actor on both sides, solo has no support. The yuri flag is emitted through its own prompt_pair_rules entry for valid distinct female/female sexual pairs.
_prompt_pair_rules_doc: Once per ActionScenePair, using its independent rule tree (mode all / first), not the unified action rules. main/support actor condition blocks, pairKind and differs are supported. main is the scene's main character, NOT the action's doer; support is the other character. Actions between the same main/support identities group across APs, commands and both directions, retaining each action's doer/receiver. distinct = different actors, self = explicit same-actor target, solo = no support; self and solo remain separate. A parent pair section has actor = main, partner = support and actions = child action sections; selected pair IDs live in pair.rules. Pair tags contain only the relative pair description, never child action prompts. $main.shortTag$ / $support.shortTag$ expand actor short tags, not workflow placeholders or group requests. No pair-rule match leaves relative output empty but retains child actions. The root mode all emits interracial and bestiality independently. Size is owned exclusively by each action's local sizeDifference option group, not by pair rules. Fixed output order is composition, complete pair groups, actors, room; no layout markers or scene output. Workflow $actions$ has one combined entry per pair: relative pair prompt, then child prompts, omitting empty text, with || between pairs.
_prompt_rules_doc: All action rules live in the ordered prompt_composite_action_rules array, including single-source families. Each rule owns its base prompts and independent options object; action roots and option records also allow optional scenePrompts arrays of strings for final scene natural language, separate from prompts. Only group and choice IDs are shared via prompt_action_option_rules; there are no shared behavior templates, references or combined variant IDs. Every local group contains exactly its complete canonical option ID set, in its own priority order. Automatic selection uses the FIRST eligible choice independently per group; a valid Build option preference tries its choice first without bypassing local predicates or view constraints. Unmatched optional groups emit nothing and inapplicable groups are omitted entirely, never injected from the registry. Selected base and option prompts are combined; every prompts value is an array of strings. Record selected option metadata as group:id on the action. Rule and choice predicates may use all/any/none and standard pairKind/main/support/differs conditions. Establish the global view from the first selected view option before rendering; later view choices respect it and other groups may test view:pov / view:external. POV camera choices require pov_possible and emit literal pov; no post-render camera cleanup or scene POV output exists. Keep nested inline {A|B|C} choices unexpanded in authored data and ComfyUI templates; runtime tag rendering may resolve each independently before comma splitting prompts, never comma-splitting scenePrompts natural language. Braces without a top-level pipe remain literal semantic markers/placeholders, including {count}, {doer} and {receiver}; do not consume them as random choices. Composition and pair rules retain independent rule-tree semantics: mode all emits every applying child; mode first emits the first applying child. Game section order is fixed: composition, pairs with actions, actors, room; final scene text includes the registry promotions and scenePrompts documented below.
_prompt_composition_rules_doc: Once per scene: the composition section, first in the fixed output order composition / pairs with child actions / actors / room. {count} = the merged count tags (futa counted as girl: 1girl, 2boys; a species named once: horse, dog; actors without species: 1other). No rule applied = the count tags alone. Composition rules and their existing prompt wording remain independent of the unified action rules.
_comfy_scene_builder_doc: Action Selector snapshots composition, pair rule definitions and scene_pair_prompts into action_data. Character registration collects short tags by node identity; Scene Builder evaluates the final registry, outputs action_prompt with unpromoted pair-relative tags and one rendered action, and outputs scene_prompt as composition followed by promoted scene-pair prompts and scenePrompts natural-language sentences. Count predicates keep girl/boy/futa separate; rendered {count} merges futa into girls. Registered actors are counted once even with both roles. Counts use shortTag, never shortName or shortPrompt. A distinct female/female sexual pair emits yuri through prompt_pair_rules, never from girl:2 alone. One-to-many role graphs have an unambiguous anchor; many-to-many graphs without source endpoints report ambiguity instead of inventing every possible pair. Local action options are finalized against actual scene facts (camera first); canonical templates and option preferences stay unchanged and inline alternatives remain unexpanded. Emotions and custom character corrections belong only to main-character prompt outputs, not support or composition.
_scene_pair_prompts_doc: FLAG -> array of prompt strings. Promote only registered flags established by actual source-derived facts or pair context.tags to the final scene output after composition and before scenePrompts natural language. Deduplicate promoted prompts scene-wide and remove only their exact matching tags from action/pair output dynamically; retain all existing derivation and pair-rule definitions. Never infer pairings from unrelated global actor tags. futa_with_female already comes from prompt_derived_tags and needs no duplicate pair derivation. Yuri is promoted for a valid derived female/female pair, not from actor counts alone. Flags omitted from this registry remain action/pair-local.

_prompt_actor_groups_doc: Deferred character detail groups. ActorPromptRule.promptGroups routes its entire output; BodyInternal_Base.promptGroups routes ordinary organ and requested trait/skill promptTags, not promptTags_always. Existing clothing/body/action checks still apply. Selected local rule and option prompts request standalone $doer.group$ / $receiver.group$ tokens; single-source rules also expose $main.group$ / $support.group$, and composites use $main.group$ / $<slot>.support.group$. The same selectors expose shortTag, shortName, shortPrompt and be (see _prompt_scene_grammar_doc); these text/grammar tokens are not deferred group requests. {doer} / {receiver} preserve the source actors' short-tag expansion; absent receivers contribute nothing. These requests add details to that actor's own prompt, not the action text; merged requests deduplicate. Known empty groups contribute nothing; unknown requests warn and are removed. Preserve requests within their individual inline pose branches, so unselected poses request nothing. Plain portraits retain flat collection. Groups express detail relevance, not geometric camera visibility.
_prompt_composite_action_rules_doc: Ordered unified array of {id, actions, distinctSupports (optional), prompts, options}, with optional all/any/none and pair conditions for rule eligibility. Rule IDs are globally unique; choice IDs are unique within their owning group. Every rule owns all its option predicates and prompt arrays; groups are independent first-match lists, not Cartesian variants. Inapplicable groups are absent, and an optional group with no match emits nothing or metadata. Each actions requirement {id, mainRole (optional), all/any/none (optional), anyOf (optional)} binds a DISTINCT raw source involving the scene main actor. Requirement base conditions must hold AND, when anyOf is present, at least one alternative must hold. Each alternative uses the same predicate shape without id, including its own optional mainRole. mainRole receiver/doer selects that side; self means an explicit same-actor target, solo means absent support; omitted mainRole is unrestricted. Backtrack over complete assignments; distinctSupports requires different real supports. Multi-source rules precede fallback single-source rules. The first eligible multi-source rule with a complete binding wins once scene-wide; suppress covered single-source poses and requests, then match remaining sources against single-source rules in priority order. No matching single rule retains an empty action record. Emit a composite once in its first requirement's pair and retain every bound source's provenance. <slot>:<tag> reads only that bound source (penetration:anal cannot borrow oral flags). Plain tags and doer:x / receiver:x are source-local for singles; unqualified composite flags aggregate only actually bound sources. Pair conditions use the first requirement's main/support pair. Record selected options as group:id metadata. Combine base prompts with selected option prompts, retaining branch-local deferred requests. $doer / $receiver / $main / $support aliases are available for singles; composites expose $main and $<slot>.support selectors. {doer} / {receiver} remain source actor placeholders.
_prompt_composite_search_doc: Check candidate sets before assignment; cap each multi-source rule at 10000 matching steps, warning and trying the next rule on exhaustion. Check rule conditions and camera view eligibility while backtracking, before resolving nested random choices. Establish the scene-wide view from the first selected option with view: pov / external before rendering; later camera groups choose only compatible choices. Other groups may test view:pov / view:external against that resolved view, regardless of group order. pov_possible is scene eligibility, not a selected view or a source action flag. Camera choices contain camera prompts; pose pools contain no camera tags. Only canonical group and option IDs are shared through prompt_action_option_rules; predicates, prompts and view behavior remain action-local, with no shared behavior templates, variant references, modifier passes or scene passes. Sleeping actor state remains separate and unchanged. Forced spitroast selects fellatio and forced through its own oral group.
_prompt_scene_prompts_schema_doc: Action root records and local option records optionally accept scenePrompts, an ARRAY of strings separate from prompts; every existing prompts value must still be an array of strings. Combine root scenePrompts with selected options' scenePrompts into final scene natural language after composition and promoted scene_pair_prompts. Do not comma-split natural-language sentences or actor descriptions. Root sentences enforce generic action-family roles, not a selected pose; no coupled-choice mechanism is needed. Preserve every inline {A|B} choice unexpanded in authored data and ComfyUI templates. Existing prompts, options, classifiers and position pools are unchanged.
_prompt_scene_grammar_doc: Text selectors use $selector.shortName$, $selector.shortPrompt$, $selector.shortTag$ and $selector.be$. shortName is authored at Template.promptProfile.shortName, never a manually inserted character/model name in action rules. shortPrompt is the classifier, optional distinct name and runtime body description parenthesized per actor; group members are individually parenthesized and joined with ' and ', not comma-split into tags. shortTag retains existing classifier/count and filtered-label semantics; counts remain shortTag-only. be resolves to is for one actual unique actor and are for multiple actual unique actors, never from words or commas in a description. Place be before the gerund and finish each sentence with a period. Single-source sentences use raw source doer/receiver aliases, following the original game COM actor direction; ComfyUI's existing roles-map compiler rewrites these aliases exactly as it does body tokens. Spitroast uses authored actDoer/actReceiver group IDs directly without inventing which support performs oral stimulation. Self-action sentences address each present role without requiring a partner; identical sentences for a shared self actor deduplicate. Grammar selectors are valid text tokens, not unknown deferred body-group requests; no new legacy raw markers are needed.
_prompt_action_option_rules_doc: Shared canonical IDs only: each group maps to an array of option IDs, never predicates, prompts or view templates. Group IDs and option IDs within each group must be valid and unique case-insensitively; local references must match canonical spelling exactly (case-sensitive). Every action using a group must declare exactly its complete option ID set; local order may vary to express priority. Inapplicable groups are omitted entirely, not added globally. All conditions, prompts, optional scenePrompts string arrays and view declarations remain action-local. Local options may use anyOf as ordered conditional branches: parent conditions must hold AND the first matching branch is selected; no matching branch makes the option ineligible. Combine inherited parent prompts with that branch's prompts, and likewise combine optional parent and branch scenePrompts arrays. Branches have no ID and do not change the parent option's canonical class or selected group:id metadata. A malformed registry or any unknown group, missing choice or extra choice rejects the entire action catalogue. Build optionPreferences uses canonical group-to-choice IDs: absent or auto preserves automatic local priority; unknown IDs warn and are ignored. A requested choice is tried first only when its local conditions and view constraints hold; otherwise normal automatic selection applies without bypassing game state. Non-futa selections use an explicit non_futa choice with empty prompts and are retained in selected option metadata.
_prompt_action_roles_doc: Each actions requirement may declare roles mapping source sides to arbitrary action-local role group IDs, e.g. {doer: actDoer, receiver: actReceiver}; these IDs are implicit per action, not a global registry or hardcoded actor identities. A matching anyOf branch may override source mappings; branches that override supply all mappings and need no base aliases. Collect members only from actual bound AP sources and deduplicate by actual actor identity. Explicit self receivers resolve to the doer; absent receivers add no member. roleID:any:tag matches any member; roleID:all:tag requires a nonempty group and every member. Both quantifiers are false for empty groups. Plain roleID:tag means any, and !tag negates the member tag test. Within a member predicate, & joins tests on the SAME actor before applying any/all: roleID:any:horse&!petite requires one non-petite horse, never a petite horse plus a different non-petite member. Filtered short-tag expansions use the same per-actor conjunction semantics: $roleID.horse&!petite$ includes only non-petite horses. $roleID.petite$ / $roleID.!petite$ expand short tags of petite / non-petite members only; $roleID.shortTag$ expands all members. These filtered short-tag expansions are action text, not deferred body-group requests. actReceiver / actDoer follow each family's authored physical role convention, not universal dominance. Spitroast merges its shared main into one actReceiver and its two distinct supports into two actDoers, including the reversed blowjob source mapping. Unity source.roles matching and source-local scopes remain unchanged.
_prompt_size_difference_doc: Every action owns all five sizeDifference choices in authored automatic priority order extremeSmallSub, extremeSmallDom, smallSub, smallDom, none. extremeSmallSub requires a petite actReceiver and a non-petite horse in actDoer (horse&!petite on the same actor); extremeSmallDom reverses these tests. Extreme choices emit size difference and extreme size difference, labeling only petite members smaller and non-petite horses larger through matching filters. A horse that is itself petite cannot count as the larger extreme actor; other species such as dog do not trigger extreme sizing unless a future author explicitly adds them. Normal smallSub has two ordered anyOf branches: first a petite non-horse actReceiver versus a non-petite actDoer, then a non-petite non-horse actReceiver versus any horse actDoer, including petite horses. smallDom mirrors these roles. Each normal choice inherits size difference and adds only its first matching branch's filtered smaller/larger labels, without interracial, bestiality or large gates. Excluding horses from the petite smaller branch prevents a petite horse being labeled smaller than an adult non-horse; the adult non-horse versus horse branch instead labels the horse larger. Extreme choices take automatic priority over normal choices; within each tier Sub precedes Dom when mixed groups allow both directions. Both uniformly petite groups (including petite horses) select none; two non-petite non-horse groups or two non-petite horse groups also select none, while a non-petite non-horse versus a horse now selects the corresponding normal choice. none is unconditional and emits no prompts, allowing an explicit preference to disable sizing. optionPreferences accepts auto / extremeSmallSub / extremeSmallDom / smallSub / smallDom / none; requested non-none choices must still pass local predicates. All 18 actions retain their local groups, including both masturbation rules: self uses the same actor on both sides and solo has an empty actDoer group, so neither produces a size difference. The selector UI node may partially defer choices until actual source bindings and actor tags are available; expose all five canonical choices without inventing partners, then resolve eligible preferences at build time.
_comfy_actor_registration_doc: ComfyUI uses explicit registrations rather than guessing actors from the game-only source role mappings. Action Selector creates an empty actor_registrations dictionary and preserves prompt_template, local option definitions, preferences and source-role audit data. Character Selector exposes ONLY two role flags: is_doer directly registers actDoer membership and is_receiver directly registers actReceiver membership; there is no second set of role flags. When building the node template, scope game aliases such as doer / receiver and source-slot aliases using each source.roles mapping to those registered action-role groups, rather than treating game source sides as universal actDoer / actReceiver identities. Unity source.roles matching remains unchanged. Each selector stores a full exported snapshot under its stable node ID; updating that node refreshes its registration, while separate nodes remain separate actors even with the same portrait ID. The action_data output retains the original template and every full registration snapshot. Its prompt output renders a private copy using all registrations so far, including size conditions and filtered actor labels; no partial result destroys the template. Chain action_data through characters and use the final node's prompt output. Inline {A|B} choices remain unexpanded. Size predicates read actor_tags, never infer petite from prompt text; re-export older records that lack body-type property tags.
